result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers credit the token set's structure, but both then list many changes rather than a few targeted gaps, so both underperform on restraint and length. A is the better answer: it has 10 items to B's 13, adds fewer speculative tokens, and says its contrast figures are estimates to check. B adds more (status tints, touch-target sizes, text-xs, px-to-rem) and states 'Checked and fine' contrast results as fact without asking for verification. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers turn a coherent v1 into a long list of additions. Neither one plainly says the set is ready to ship. B is a bit better: it opens by naming the strengths of the structure, makes fewer suggestions, and says its contrast numbers are hand estimates to check. A states 'checked and fine' contrast results as fact and suggests broader changes, such as switching spacing to rem and adding touch-target and density tokens.
